stem:
$A^{-}(g) \rightarrow A^{2 +}(g)$ $\Delta H = 1100\ KJ/mol$
$A(g) \rightarrow A^{2 +}(g)$ $\Delta H = 1200\ KJ/mol$
Electron gain enthalphy of A is $P \times 10^{2}KJ/mol$. What is the
value of P ?
solution:
$A(g) + e^{-} \rightarrow A^{-}(g)$
$\Delta H = + E \cdot G \cdot E$....(1)
$A(g) \rightarrow A^{2 +}(g) + 2e^{-}$ $\Delta H = 1200\ KJ/mol$....(2)
$A^{-}(g) \rightarrow A^{2 +}(g) + 3e^{-}$ $\Delta H = 1100\ KJ/mol$....(3)
Eq. (3) = (2) - (1)
$- E \cdot G \cdot E + 1200 = 1100$
$- E \cdot G \cdot E = - 100\ KJ/mol$
$P = 1$.

The standard electrode
potential$E^{0}$for$Fe^{+ + +} + e^{-} \rightarrow Fe^{+ +}$ is
solution:
$\Delta G^{\circ} = - nE^{0}F$
$Fe^{2 +} + 2e^{-} \rightarrow Fe$....(i)
$\Delta G^{0} = - 2 \times F \times ( - 0.440V) = 0.880F$
$Fe^{3 +} + 3e^{-} \rightarrow Fe$....(ii)
$\Delta G^{\circ} = - 3 \times F \times ( - 0.036) = 0.108F$
On subtracting equation (i) from (ii)
${Fe}^{3 +} + e^{-} \rightarrow {Fe}^{2 +}$
$\Delta G^{\circ} = 0.108F - 0.880F = - 0.772F$
$E^{0}$for the reaction$= - \frac{\Delta G^{\circ}}{nF}$
$= - \frac{( - 0.772F)}{1 \times F} = + 0.772V$

stem:
The wavelength of a moving body of mass 0.1 mg is 3.31 × 10-29
m. The kinetic energy of the body in J would be
solution:
$\lambda = \frac{h}{mv}$
$mv = \frac{h}{\lambda}$
$m^{2}v^{2} = \frac{h^{2}}{m\lambda^{2}}$
$\frac{1}{2}{mv}^{2} = \frac{h^{2}}{2m\lambda^{2}}$
$KE = \frac{h^{2}}{2m\lambda^{2}} = \frac{\left( 6.6 \times 10^{- 34} \right)^{2}}{2 \times 10^{- 4} \times \left( 3.31 \times 10^{- 29} \right)^{2}} = 2 \times 10^{- 6}$
